findings.title: Recheck the tick budget immediately before spawning a run
findings.description: `_act` checks the budget before calling `_launch`, but `_launch` then mints the ID, builds arguments, and writes the journal entry before `launch()` calls `Popen`. If that work crosses the deadline—or a stop is requested during it—the subprocess still starts after the budget should have refused it. Check the budget again at the actual spawn boundary, before `Popen`, and avoid leaving a newly journaled entry without an intentional outcome if the check refuses the call.

findings.title: Propagate store integrity failures instead of treating them as project faults
findings.description: `STORE_FAILURES` omits `StoreIntegrityError`, even though store operations raise it when a database invariant is violated. `RunnerTenant._tick_project` only propagates the listed store failures; this exception therefore falls through to the broad catch and is handled as an ordinary unexpected project fault, allowing the process to continue after a store integrity failure. Include this typed store failure in the propagate set so the process stops rather than treating the store as usable.

findings.title: Add a load test for the Runner’s subprocess and multi-project path
findings.description: The new Runner performs bounded `sq` and `cf` subprocess calls and ticks multiple projects, but the existing load-test tier contains no Runner coverage. Unit and end-to-end tests exercise functional behavior and deadline checks, but do not establish throughput, latency, or resource bounds with a realistic mix of projects and in-flight runs. The Python testing rules require a gated load test for network, concurrency, or environment-layer paths.
